skill.name: list-hygiene-monitor
skill.description: Monitors email list hygiene over time by cohorting engagement recency, trending bounces and complaints, checking suppression drift, and producing re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists. Use it for recurring list health reviews, not authentication pre-flight checks or final SEND quality scoring.
skill.summary: Monitor email list decay and build segmented re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans and repo-relative links, not executable Ruby backticks or path traversal. One medium finding remains confirmed because the skill documents optional python3 connector commands that read ESP subscriber and event data.

remediation.issue: Optional connector commands access live ESP contact and event data.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running connector commands, and summarize what data will be read before execution.

remediation.issue: Saved report filenames include a user-facing list or topic placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize list names into safe slugs before writing memory files, and keep writes inside memory/email/list-hygiene-monitor/.

content.value_statement: Aging lists reduce engagement and increase bounce or complaint risk. This skill turns ESP exports and prior baselines into clear cohorts, trend reads, and action worklists.
actual_capabilities: Groups subscribers into 30, 90, 180, and 365 day engagement cohorts.
Compares hard bounce and spam complaint rates against benchmarks and prior baselines.
Checks suppression-list growth and flags possible opt-out leakage for auditor review.
Builds segmented re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists with measured or estimated counts.
Produces SEND list-hygiene and engagement-decay reads for handoff to email-quality-auditor.
Can use keyless exports, prior reports, or optional ESP connector outputs when available.
limitations: It does not run authentication or DNS deliverability pre-flight checks.
It does not own consent records or change suppression status by itself.
It does not compute the final EQS score or enforce SEND vetoes.
Trend accuracy depends on clean ESP exports and a comparable prior baseline.

use_cases.title: Review Monthly List Health
use_cases.description: Track engagement decay, bounce movement, and complaint trends before the next campaign cycle.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Win-Back Segment
use_cases.description: Identify dormant subscribers who should receive a re-permission or reactivation campaign.

use_cases.title: Audit Suppression Drift
use_cases.description: Compare opt-out history with the active send list and route leakage concerns to the auditor.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Hygiene Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review with one current export.
prompt_templates.prompt: Watch my list health for [program]. Here is my ESP engagement export and bounce report. Cohort subscribers and build a prune worklist.

prompt_templates.title: Baseline Trend Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare current health against a prior run.
prompt_templates.prompt: Trend this list against last quarter. Use the current export, bounce and complaint report, and baseline file. Show deltas and needed actions.

prompt_templates.title: Suppression Drift Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on opt-out and suppression consistency.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check suppression drift for [list]. Compare active subscribers with the opt-out history and identify leakage, growth, and reconciliation issues.

prompt_templates.title: Full SEND Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the scheduled hygiene monitor for [program]. Include cohorts, bounce and complaint trends, suppression drift, action worklists, SEND S and E reads, and the handoff summary.

output_examples.input: A current ESP engagement export, a bounce report, and no prior baseline.
output: Engagement cohorts labeled measured or estimated, with dormant and deep-dormant counts.
Point-in-time bounce and complaint rates, with the trend marked needs input.
A re-permission, sunset, and prune worklist sized by cohort.

output_examples.input: A monthly export plus a prior hygiene report for the same list.
output: Run-over-run deltas for dormant load, hard bounces, complaints, and suppression growth.
Plain-language flags for rising risk and recommended send-hold review when needed.
A concise handoff for email-quality-auditor with SEND S and E evidence.

output_examples.input: An active list and a suppression or opt-out history export.
output: Suppression growth summary and possible leakage examples.
Addresses or segments that should be removed, suppressed, or reconciled.
Open loops for consent-registry or auditor follow-up.

best_practices: Use comparable export windows and the same list definition for each scheduled run.
Label every cohort and rate as measured or estimated, especially when source data is partial.
Route suppression leakage and over-benchmark trends to the auditor before sending again.
anti_patterns: Do not invent trend deltas when no prior baseline is available.
Do not re-mail complainers, hard bounces, or suppressed contacts through re-permission campaigns.
Do not treat the hygiene worklist as the final EQS verdict.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs an ESP engagement export, bounce and complaint data, a prior baseline when available, and suppression history.

faq.question: Can it work without per-subscriber data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use cohort-level counts or rates, but it must label those outputs as estimated.

faq.question: Does it update my suppression list?
faq.answer: No. It identifies drift and leakage, then hands record changes to the consent registry workflow.

faq.question: Does it decide if a campaign can send?
faq.answer: No. It provides SEND S and E evidence, while email-quality-auditor makes the final verdict.

faq.question: How often should I run it?
faq.answer: Use monthly checks for high-frequency programs, quarterly checks for newsletters, and per-cycle checks for cold outbound.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill hosts.
